desc:
An undirected graph has n nodes numbered 0 to n - 1. Each entry edges[i] = [a, b] is a connection between nodes a and b.

The distance of a node from src is the fewest connections you must follow to get there. Return an array sizes where sizes[d] is the number of nodes whose distance from src is exactly d. The array ends at the largest distance that occurs; nodes that cannot be reached from src are not counted anywhere.

n = 7, src = 0
edges = [[0,1], [0,2], [1,3], [2,3], [3,4], [5,6]]
-> [1, 2, 1, 1]

Node 0 is at distance 0, nodes 1 and 2 at distance 1, node 3 at distance 2 and node 4 at distance 3. Nodes 5 and 6 are in a different component.
constraints: 0 ≤ a, b < n, a ≠ b, and no pair of nodes is listed twice
hints: The distance of a node is exactly the round in which a breadth-first search first reaches it.
Run BFS from src but process the queue one round at a time: everything currently in the queue belongs to the same distance.
Keep a list for the current level. Record its length, then build the next level from the unvisited neighbours of the current one. Stop when the next level is empty.
editorial: Build adjacency lists, mark src as visited and put it in the first level. Repeat: append the size of the current level to the answer, then collect every not-yet-visited neighbour of the level's nodes (marking them visited as you add them) into the next level. The loop ends when a level comes out empty.

A node is added the first time any node of the previous level touches it, and by the layered nature of BFS that is exactly its shortest distance. Every node and edge is looked at a constant number of times, so the time is O(n + m).
